The epitope-specific nanobody was demonstrated to form a complex with S. capitis divalent metal ion transporter protein (ScaDMT) and truncated ScaDMT(tru) by gel filtration. In the ScaDMT(tru) construct, 41 amino acids from the N terminus were removed, including 17 residues of the first predicted transmembrane helix. This construct was stable, and it transported Cd2+ and Mn2+ and bound Cd2+ with similar affinity (Kd = 37 ± 8 μM) to that of wild type, thus ensuring that the functional properties of the truncated protein were retained.

The epitope of the nanobody anti-ScaDMT on the truncated S. capitis divalent metal ion transporter protein (ScaDMT(tru)) was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. The nanobody was used as a crystallization chaperone. In the ScaDMT(tru) construct, 41 amino acids from the N terminus were removed, including 17 residues of the first predicted transmembrane helix. This construct was stable, and it transported Cd2+ and Mn2+ and bound Cd2+ with similar affinity (Kd = 37 ± 8 μM) to that of wild type, thus ensuring that the functional properties of the truncated protein were retained. There are two copies of the ScaDMT(tru)-nanobody complex in the asymmetric unit.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.1 angstroms
